Device memory layouts

Source: R/experimental_layout.R
experimental_layout_Layout.Rd

Ports of jax.experimental.layout.Layout, Layout.AUTO, Layout.for_array, Layout.update and Format. A layout lists the dimensions of an array from the most major to the most minor (0 based): c(0, 1) is the row major order of a matrix and c(1, 0) the column major one. experimental_layout_Layout_AUTO lets the compiler choose. A Format pairs a layout with a sharding; jaxR runs on one device, so the sharding is NULL or a device name from devices().

Usage

experimental_layout_Layout(
  major_to_minor,
  tiling = NULL,
  sub_byte_element_size_in_bits = 0L
)

experimental_layout_Layout_AUTO

experimental_layout_Layout_for_array(x)

experimental_layout_Layout_update(x, ...)

experimental_layout_Format(layout = NULL, sharding = NULL)

Arguments

major_to_minor

Integer vector, a permutation of 0:(ndim - 1).

tiling

NULL or a list of integer vectors (tiles). The CPU device has no tiled layouts, so only NULL and the empty list can be used in a computation.

sub_byte_element_size_in_bits

Integer.

x

An array (for for_array) or a layout (for update).

...

Fields to replace (major_to_minor, tiling, sub_byte_element_size_in_bits).

layout

NULL, experimental_layout_Layout_AUTO or a layout.

sharding

NULL or a device name.

Value

A jax_Layout or jax_Format object.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
l <- experimental_layout_Layout(c(1L, 0L))
l
experimental_layout_Layout_for_array(jnp_ones(c(2L, 3L)))
experimental_layout_Format(l, devices()[1])
} # }
